title: Activation steward daily ops scratchpad
body:
Purpose: quick, actionable checklist and comms matrix for the activation steward during small-to-medium canary and A/B exposures. This is a working scratchpad — use for daily run-of-show and signal triage.

Context: product console teams run progressive exposure for model changes and feature flags. We need a compact steward runbook that fits on one screen for on-call coverage and rotation handoffs. Not a replacement for the full staged-rollout playbook; this is the live ops companion.

Scope:
- Target: feature toggles, model variant swaps, reranker/lm parameter rollouts up to 10% traffic.
- Excludes infra-level capacity scaling (SRE handles >50% lane changes).

Steward role (primary): A simple breakdown, what to do first, and who to ping.
- Triage and surface deviations in first 15 minutes after change.
- Validate experiment identity + traffic slices (cohort mapping).
- Make go/no-go calls for immediate rollback if critical signals hit.
- Coordinate cross-functional comms (eng, product, SRE, CS).

Daily run-of-show (pre-exposure) checklist (15–30 min before activation):
- Confirm experiment ID and rollout config matches PR and ticket (verify sample size, slice selector).
- Verify baseline traffic routing: staging -> shadow -> canary slices.
- Smoke tests: 10 scripted queries (short list included below) against canary variant.
- Telemetry sanity: dashboards up, threshold notifications enabled, retention windows set to 30m for immediate signals.
- Pager routing: ensure oncall SRE and ML infra are subscribed.
- Stakeholder comms: post start ETA in #release-coordination, add experiment to daily standup board.

Activation minute-zero checklist (0–15m):
- Mark start time in experiment log: local timestamp + UTC.
- Watch latency p50/p95, error rate, token-generation timeout spikes.
- Check cost-exposure gauge if enabled (approx token cost delta).
- Confirm sample assignment distribution looks like expected.
- Run smoke queries and inspect model outputs for obvious regressions (hallucination, prompt truncation).

Primary signals and thresholds (fast fail if any tripped):
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline in 10m window -> FAIL
- Latency p95 increase > 200ms relative -> WARN; > 500ms -> FAIL
- User-facing correctness regressions (human-feedback or small eval set mismatch) > 3% -> FAIL
- Abnormal token-cost delta > 15% -> INVESTIGATE (possible misconfig/quantization mismatch)
- Dropped KV cache hit rate > 10% -> WARN

Escalation matrix (who to ping by priority):
- Tier 1 (immediate): steward -> assigned eng oncall (channel @eng-oncall)
- Tier 2: if infra-related (GPU OOMs, model crashes) escalate to SRE lead and infra-ml (pager)
- Tier 3: product PM and CS for high-severity user-impacting regressions

Communication templates (short messages to paste into Slack):
- Start: "[ROLL-212] canary start: model v2 -> v2-quantized; slice: EU-beta ~2% traffic. Steward: Aisha. DASH: <link>. Will monitor 30m."
- WARN: "[ROLL-212] WARN: p95 latency +230ms vs baseline (10m). Observed increased tail. Investigating; SRE looped in."
- FAIL / Rollback: "[ROLL-212] ROLLBACK: trigger=error-rate. Rolling back to v1. Steps: disable route -> confirm traffic restored -> postmortem ticket ROLL-212-PM."

Rollback quick steps (fast path):
- Disable canary routing at control plane (console route toggle).
- If control plane unresponsive, activate traffic fallback rule via infra CLI (runbook link).
- Validate that traffic flows back to pinned stable variant and latency/error rates return to baseline.
- Notify stakeholders in Slack + send incident stub to #incidents.

Post-decision (after 30–60m stable):
- If stable: schedule extended monitoring (next 24h telemetry summary), annotate experiment with confirmation + any mitigations.
- If rollback: create postmortem stub, assign root-cause owner, capture traces and full raw request samples for 2h window around event, schedule deep-dive.

Triage heuristics (fast mental checklist for steward):
- Is signal correlated with traffic spike/time zone? If yes, consider transient noise.
- Is degradation tied to specific cohort? If yes, quarantine slice and limit exposure.
- Are SLOs breached or are we seeing new failure modes not captured by alerts? If new, escalate immediately.

Simple smoke query set (run through vanity harness):
- Short completion: "Summarize in one sentence" x 3 prompts
- Safety prompt: edge-case toxic content -> check filter pass/fail
- Instruction compliance: structured output expected -> verify field presence
- Latency-sensitive: 512 token synthetic prompt -> measure tail latency

Open questions / TODOs (this doc is a scratchpad):
- Add automated hypothesis logger that stamps metrics correlation to cohort (TODO @Liam).
- Formalize cost-threshold escalations into alerting rules (current cost flagging is manual).
- Need a small mobile-friendly dashboard for stewards on-call (low-dev effort).

Quick links:
- Full rollout playbook (confluence): pg/rollout-playbook
- Experiment tracker: https://pm.redwood/exp/Roll-212
- Telemetry dashboard (fast): https://grafana.redwood/d/rollout-fastview
- Smoke script: github.com/redwood/qa/rollout-smoke (PR #23)

Notes to self (informal):
- keep this doc lean. if a pattern repeats (eg: latency at 2% exposures), promote to canonical checklist.
- in handoffs, always include last 30m snapshot + any manual mitigations applied.

End.
